## Solution

**Interpreting the equation.** The left side lists the even shifts $0,2,4,\dots,2016,2018$ with coefficients $\binom{2018}{0},\binom{2018}{2},\dots,\binom{2018}{2016},\binom{2018}{2018}$ (the printed "$2106$" being a typo for $2016$), and the right side lists the odd shifts $1,3,\dots,2015,2017$ with coefficients $\binom{2018}{1},\binom{2018}{3},\dots,\binom{2018}{2015},\binom{2018}{2017}$ (the printed "$2105,2107$" being typos for $2015,2017$). Thus the equation is

$$\sum_{k=0}^{2018}(-1)^{k}\binom{2018}{k}P(x+k)=0\qquad(\forall x\in\mathbb R). \tag{1}$$

**Finite differences.** Let $\Delta P(x)=P(x+1)-P(x)$ be the forward difference. By the binomial theorem for operators,

$$\Delta^{n}P(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-k}\binom{n}{k}P(x+k),$$

so $\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-1)^{k}\binom{n}{k}P(x+k)=(-1)^{n}\Delta^{n}P(x)$. Since $n=2018$ is even, (1) is equivalent to

$$\Delta^{2018}P(x)\equiv 0. \tag{2}$$

**Degree drop lemma.** If $P$ has degree $d\ge 1$ with leading coefficient $a_d$, then
$$P(x+1)-P(x)=a_d\bigl((x+1)^d-x^d\bigr)+\cdots=a_d\,d\,x^{d-1}+\cdots,$$
so $\Delta P$ has degree exactly $d-1$. Iterating, $\Delta^{d}P$ is the nonzero constant $d!\,a_d$, and $\Delta^{d+1}P\equiv 0$.

**Conclusion.** By the lemma, $\Delta^{2018}P\equiv 0$ holds exactly when $2018>\deg P$, i.e. when $\deg P\le 2017$. Conversely, every polynomial of degree $\le 2017$ satisfies (2), hence (1).

Therefore the polynomials satisfying the given identity are precisely

$$\boxed{\,P\in\mathbb R[x]\ \text{with}\ \deg P\le 2017\,}.$$
